evals.name: new-initiative-from-scratch
evals.prompt: we keep getting asked for shared team workspaces - right now Cadence is one flat schedule per company and bigger customers (the 20-30 seat ones) keep emailing support asking to split it by department because the sales team schedule is drowning out engineering. i want to write up the scope properly before anyone touches code. can you do that? assume i'm the only one deciding, target is end of Q1.
evals.expected_output: A numbered PRD at docs/prd/0002-<slug>.md with explicit non-goals, numbered testable requirements, measurable success metrics with baseline+target, and phased scope. Should not contain schemas, endpoints, or component names.
assertions: Creates exactly one new PRD file at docs/prd/0002-<slug>.md (correct next number, 4-digit, lowercase-hyphen slug)
Leaves the existing docs/prd/0001-enterprise-tier.md untouched
Has a ## Non-Goals section with at least 2 concrete, specific exclusions (not 'TBD' or generic filler)
Functional requirements are numbered with FR-N IDs and carry MUST/SHOULD/MAY priorities
Success metrics include a real baseline AND a target number, not placeholder brackets
Has a ## Scope by Phase section where phase 1 is a genuinely shippable smallest version
Contains no implementation detail: no SQL/DDL, no API endpoint paths, no component or file names
YAML front matter present with prd, title, status, owner, created, updated
Whole PRD is under 400 lines (scope stayed one initiative)
Assumptions the agent made on the user's behalf are stated explicitly in the reply

evals.name: amend-cut-requirement
evals.prompt: ok change of plan on enterprise. SCIM is dead for this year, we're not doing it - the two design partners both said manual invites are fine at their size. also legal came back and says the audit log has to be kept 7 years not 90 days, thats non negotiable now. update the doc.
evals.expected_output: docs/prd/0001-enterprise-tier.md edited in place: FR-2 (SCIM) removed from requirements or marked cut and moved to Non-Goals, audit log 7-year retention added as a requirement, updated: date bumped, and two new Changelog rows with reasons. Filename and prd number unchanged. No new PRD file created.
assertions: Edits docs/prd/0001-enterprise-tier.md in place — filename, prd number, and created date unchanged
Creates no new file under docs/prd/
SCIM is no longer a MUST requirement: removed from the FR table or explicitly moved to Non-Goals
7-year audit log retention is captured as a requirement or NFR with the 7-year figure
Front matter updated: field is bumped to 2026-09-11
At least 2 new Changelog rows dated 2026-09-11, each with a stated reason (design-partner feedback, legal)
Scope by Phase table no longer schedules the cut SCIM requirement
Body reads as current truth — no strikethrough, no 'EDIT:'/'UPDATE:' inline annotations left in sections
Flags the downstream impact (that .design/enterprise-tier/ may now contradict the PRD)

evals.name: scope-too-small
evals.prompt: write me a PRD for adding a dark mode toggle in the settings page
evals.expected_output: Names the cheaper path first (the real work is de-hardcoding colors / a token layer, not the toggle) in about a sentence, then writes a SHORT PRD anyway — core sections only, no Stakeholders, no Rollout, no phases. Invents no metrics or stakeholders; an unknown baseline is written as 'unknown — how to get it'.
assertions: Writes docs/prd/0002-<slug>.md — does not refuse, since the user asked for the doc
Doc is short (roughly under 100 lines) and omits the extended sections: no Stakeholders, no Rollout, no Dependencies, no Scope by Phase
Names the cheaper/real path up front (token layer or de-hardcoding colors is the actual work, not the toggle)
Fabricates nothing: any missing baseline is written as unknown with how to get it, and no stakeholder is invented for a solo decider
Captures the decisions that actually get argued later (light/dark/system default, where the preference is stored, app-wide vs one page)
